title: Poison Ivy Gizy snags inaugural CODM GBRC 2026 trophy
summary: MANILA, Philippines — Filipino team Poison Ivy Gizy captured the first-ever Call of Duty: Mobile (CODM) Garena Battle Royale Cup championship after dominating the two-day Grand Finals inside the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Filipino team Poison Ivy Gizy captured the first-ever Call of Duty: Mobile (CODM) Garena Battle Royale Cup championship after dominating the two-day Grand Finals inside the Ayala Malls Manila Bay Activity Center on November 7–8, 2026.
The grand finals format that upped the stakes higher
The 10-team finals cast brought together seven squads from the GBRC Online Playoffs alongside regional champions from Indonesia, Thailand, and Taiwan/Hong Kong/Macau.
The finale also featured a high-stakes “Endgame Protocol” format, which departs from the traditional leaderboard and cumulative standings to decide the winning team.
Moving away from traditional cumulative leaderboards, the finale introduced a high-stakes “Endgame Protocol” format.
Under this new rule, the championship-eligibility threshold is automatically set 10 points higher than the top team’s score at the end of Day 1.
Filipino team Poison Ivy Gizy topped the charts after the first day of the games, racking up 106 points to establish the tournament target score at 116 points.
To become “In The Zone” and be eligible for the championship, teams had to either surpass the target score or claim a Zone Bounty by eliminating a player from an active “In The Zone” team.
Once a team earns the special status, the tournament shifts into a race to the finish line.
From Map 8 onward, the first championship-eligible team to secure a map victory is immediately declared the tournament champions, and any remaining scheduled maps are canceled.

Entering the second day as title favorites, Poison Ivy only needed two more maps to secure the status and eventually the inaugural championship of the Garena-backed Battle Royale tournament after winning Map 8.

Secre shines through

blocks.caption: Secre wins Finals MVP honors. Photo by Clyde Jan Pascual

blocks.text: Gabrielle Paolo “Secre” Diaz took home the Finals MVP honors as he helped the squad to become one of only two teams to achieve two map wins in the offline finals—along with LEAP Main, who finished fourth in the tournamen.
“I was not really expecting to win the MVP honors, as I thought that would be won by either Leigh or Drei,” Secre mentioned.
He also shared that their daily grinds, scrimmages, and competing in community tournaments helped them prepare for their matches during the group stage and the playoffs.
“We struggled during our run in the tournament, but we still kept on getting to the top of the leaderboards,” he added.
Secre also grabbed a 30,000 COD Points (CP) bonus for winning the special award.
Aside from Secre, completing the championship-clinching lineup included Marc Andrie “Drie” Salazar, Niño “Vrus” Salonga, Bernard Dalton “Void” Patayon, and Aldred Give “Leigh” Malicdem.
For Vrus, he wished for more international tournaments, as they are ready to show their grit on the global stage.

“I think what’s missing for us is the international tournaments—where we can fight against global teams, and I hope that Garena will have more international tournaments. We’re ready to give our all just to get the championship in international,” Vrus shared during the post-match interview.

The squad took home US$14,000 as champions, while GNR Esports Legacy Omen secured a runner-up finish taking US$6,000, and completing the podium were Matikas Synergy Force (M12 SYN Main team), earning US$4,000.
